title: Bounded finite-projective product-Hom dual involution
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring and $P$ an integer cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], zero outside $[a,b]$ for integers $a\leq b$, with finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] terms. Write $O=B[0]$ and $H$ for the product total module Hom complex [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Put $E=H(P,O)$ and $F=H(E,O)$. Projection to the sole possibly nonzero product coordinate gives natural module isomorphisms $E^r\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(P^{-r},B)$ and $F^p\cong(P^p)^{**}$, where $M^*=\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,B)$. Under these identifications $d_E^r(\phi)=(-1)^{r+1}\phi d_P^{-r-1}$ and $d_F^p=-(d_P^p)^{**}$; $E$ vanishes outside $[-b,-a]$ and has finitely generated projective terms. The homogeneous formula $\delta_P(x)(\phi)=(-1)^{p q}\phi(x)$ for $x\in P^p$, $\phi\in E^q$, $p+q=0$, with zero in all other Hom coordinates, defines a chain isomorphism $\delta_P:P\xrightarrow{\sim}F$. Its component in degree $p$ is $(-1)^p\operatorname{ev}_{P^p}$ and its inverse component is $(-1)^p\operatorname{ev}_{P^p}^{-1}$, where $\operatorname{ev}_M(x)(\phi)=\phi(x)$. These chain isomorphisms are natural in chain maps between such complexes: $H(H(f,O),O)\delta_P=\delta_{P'}f$ for $f:P\to P'$.

proof.text: By [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], $E^r=\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}_B(P^i,O^{i+r})$. For $i\ne-r$ the target is zero, so projection to $i=-r$ is an isomorphism with inverse inserting a map at $-r$ and zero elsewhere. Likewise $F^p\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(E^{-p},B)\cong(P^p)^{**}$. Projection and insertion commute with precomposition, so these module identifications are natural. If $r\notin[-b,-a]$, then $P^{-r}=0$, hence $E^r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes; Tag 0FNG, section-sign-rules, item-evaluation; Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: The differential of $O=B[0]$ is zero. Substituting in the differential of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], the coordinate at $i=-r-1$ of $d_E^r(\phi)$ is $-(-1)^r\phi\circ d_P^{-r-1}=(-1)^{r+1}\phi\circ d_P^{-r-1}$. All other coordinates have zero target. This proves the asserted first differential formula.

source.place: Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes; Tag 0FNG, section-sign-rules, item-evaluation; Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: Apply the same differential formula to $F=H(E,O)$. For $u\in F^p=(P^p)^{**}$ and $\psi\in E^{-p-1}=(P^{p+1})^*$, Step 2 gives $d_F^p(u)(\psi)=(-1)^{p+1}u(d_E^{-p-1}\psi)=(-1)^{p+1}(-1)^{-p}u(\psi\circ d_P^p)=-u(\psi\circ d_P^p)$. By the definition of double transpose, this is $-(d_P^p)^{**}(u)(\psi)$. Equality on every $\psi$ proves the asserted second differential formula.

source.place: Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes; Tag 0FNG, section-sign-rules, item-evaluation; Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: For every integer $r$, the hypotheses make $P^{-r}$ a finitely generated projective $B$-module. Apply [lem-sf-finite-projective-dual] to this module: its dual is finitely generated and projective. The projection isomorphism of Step 1 therefore proves these properties for $E^r$. Together with its support calculation this proves the bounded finite-projectivity assertion.

source.place: Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes; Tag 0FNG, section-sign-rules, item-evaluation; Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: Define $\delta_P^p(x)$ by inserting $(-1)^p\operatorname{ev}_{P^p}(x)$ in the sole coordinate $E^{-p}\to B$, and zero elsewhere. This is $B$-linear. If $q=-p$, then $pq=-p^2\equiv p\pmod2$, so its value on $\phi\in E^q$ is precisely $(-1)^{pq}\phi(x)$. For $x\in P^p$ and $\psi\in(P^{p+1})^*$, Step 3 yields $d_F^p(\delta_P^p x)(\psi)=(-1)^{p+1}\psi(d_P^p x)=\delta_P^{p+1}(d_P^p x)(\psi)$. Extensionality and Step 1 give the chain-map identity in every degree.

source.place: Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes; Tag 0FNG, section-sign-rules, item-evaluation; Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: Apply the evaluation-isomorphism clause of [lem-sf-finite-projective-dual] to each $P^p$. Since $(-1)^p(-1)^p=1$, the component $\eta^p=(-1)^p\operatorname{ev}_{P^p}^{-1}:F^p\to P^p$ satisfies $\eta^p\delta_P^p=1$ and $\delta_P^p\eta^p=1$. Multiplying the chain identity $d_F^p\delta_P^p=\delta_P^{p+1}d_P^p$ on the left by $\eta^{p+1}$ and on the right by $\eta^p$ gives $\eta^{p+1}d_F^p=d_P^p\eta^p$. Thus $\eta$ is a chain map and a two-sided inverse, proving the specified chain isomorphism and inverse formula.

source.place: Tag 0A8H, section-hom-complexes; Tag 0FNG, section-sign-rules, item-evaluation; Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, first paragraph of proof.

proof.text: Let $f:P\to P'$ be a chain map and put $E'=H(P',O)$. Precomposition gives $H(f,O)^r(\phi')=\phi'\circ f^{-r}$; its chain identity follows by replacing $d_{P'}f$ by $fd_P$ in Step 2. Applying precomposition twice therefore gives $H(H(f,O),O)^p(u)(\phi')=u(\phi'\circ f^p)$ for $\phi'\in E'^{-p}$. At $u=\delta_P^p(x)$ this equals $(-1)^p\phi'(f^p x)=\delta_{P'}^p(f^p x)(\phi')$. Equality in every coordinate proves $H(H(f,O),O)\delta_P=\delta_{P'}f$.
